title: First coherent cohomology dimension of an abelian variety
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety] of dimension $g$. Then $\dim_k H^1(A,\mathcal O_A)=g$, where $H^1$ is Zariski sheaf cohomology of the structure sheaf.

source.place: Chapter I, Remark 8.7(e), printed p.37: coherent-cohomology dimension input underlying the dimension assertion; see also Mumford, Abelian Varieties, coherent cohomology of abelian varieties (WANTED for its proof).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization] and [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective], $A$ is geometrically integral and projective. Put $H^q=H^q(A,\mathcal O_A)$ and $h=\dim_kH^1$. Proper coherent finiteness [lem-fin-proper-coherent-finite-dimensional] makes each $H^q$ finite dimensional. The scheme is Noetherian, since it is of finite type over the field $k$. Thus [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^q=0$ for $q>g$. Also $H^0=k$ by [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety].

source.place: I Remark 8.7(e), printed p.37; I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55, with coherent finiteness and Stacks 02UZ for the coherent degree bound

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-coherent-group-bialgebra] on $A$. Its coproduct has every element of $H^1$ primitive. If $h>g$, choose $g+1$ members of a basis of $H^1$. By [lem-sfb-graded-primitive-product] their product is a nonzero element of $H^{g+1}$, contradicting step 1. Consequently $h\leq g$. This uses the ordered-product assertion, so in characteristic two it requires neither division by a factorial nor a separate assertion that degree-one squares vanish.

source.place: I Lemma 12.2, printed p.55: degree-one bound, adapted to coherent cohomology

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-picard-identity-representability] to $(A,0)$, and call its proper connected identity component $P$. It is a separated finite-type group scheme and represents rigidified algebraically trivial families; its universal sheaf is trivial on both identity axes. Crucially the cited statement gives $T_0P\cong H^1(A,\mathcal O_A)$ without assuming $P$ smooth or reduced. We will only need $\dim P\leq h$, not smoothness of $P$.

source.place: I Remark 8.7(e), printed p.37, and the general projective Picard input recorded by the cited auxiliary

proof.text: Choose an ample invertible sheaf $L$ using [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective]. On $A_x\times A_y$ form $N=m^*L\otimes p_1^*L^{-1}\otimes p_2^*L^{-1}\otimes c^*(0^*L)$, where $c$ is the structure map. Cancellation trivializes both identity axes. The family, with parameter the smooth connected $A_y$, connects each fibre to the trivial fibre; hence its fibres are algebraically trivial. Representability [lem-sfb-projective-picard-identity-representability] gives $f:A\to P$ with $N\cong(1\times f)^*\mathcal P$. By [thm-sc-theorem-of-cube], $N(x,y+z)\cong N(x,y)\otimes N(x,z)$ as families rigidified at $x=0$: the quotient is the seven-factor cube expression $L_{x+y+z}L_xL_yL_z/(L_{x+y}L_{x+z}L_{y+z})$, with its constant identity-line factor cancelled by normalization. Uniqueness in representability gives $f(y+z)=f(y)+f(z)$ and $f(0)=0$ as morphisms of schemes. Thus $f$ is a homomorphism.

source.place: I Theorem 5.5 and Remark 5.6; I section 8, normalized L* construction, printed pp.39–40

proof.text: The kernel $K=f^{-1}(0)$ is a closed subgroup, since $P$ is separated. Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-closed-subgroup-reduced-component]: $B=(K_{\mathrm{red}})^0$ is an abelian subvariety and $\dim B=\dim K$. As $f|_B=0$, the representing equality for $N$ and the trivial zero fibre of the universal sheaf show that $N|_{A\times B}$ is trivial. Restrict further to $B\times B$ and pull back by $x\mapsto(x,-x)$. Since addition on this map is zero, cancellation yields $L|_B\otimes[-1]^*(L|_B)\cong\mathcal O_B$, up to a constant one-dimensional factor, which is trivial over $k$.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1, printed p.35: the connected reduced kernel and its restricted ample sheaf

proof.text: The restriction $L|_B$ is ample in the complete-linear-system convention [def-sc-ample]. Indeed choose $L^{\otimes m}$ very ample on $A$, and restrict its embedding to the closed subscheme $B$, obtaining $i:B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N$ defined by generating sections $s_0,\ldots,s_N$ of $M=L^{\otimes m}|_B$. By [lem-fin-proper-coherent-finite-dimensional], $V=H^0(B,M)$ is finite dimensional. The quotient $V\otimes\mathcal O_B\twoheadrightarrow M$ defines $j:B\to\mathbf P(V^\vee)$ by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. The linear map $k^{N+1}\to V$ defined by the $s_i$ gives a projection $\pi$ on the open where they generate, containing $j(B)$; quotient functoriality gives $i=\pi j$. Hence $j$ is a monomorphism: equality after $j$ implies equality after $i$. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated], and therefore a closed immersion by [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed]. This proves $M$ very ample and $L|_B$ ample. The inverse automorphism of $B$ also pulls its complete linear embedding back to an embedding, so $[-1]^*(L|_B)$ is ample.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1, printed p.35: restriction of an ample bundle; complete-system details supplied by the agent

proof.text: By [lem-sc-ample-tensor], the trivial bundle in step 5 is ample on $B$. If $\dim B>0$ this is impossible: $B$ is proper geometrically integral by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], so [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] gives $H^0(B,\mathcal O_B)=k$. Every complete linear system of a power of the trivial bundle therefore maps $B$ to $\mathbf P^0$, and cannot be a closed immersion from a positive-dimensional scheme. This contradicts [def-sc-ample]. Thus $\dim B=0$, and [lem-sfb-abelian-closed-subgroup-reduced-component] implies that $K$ is finite, including its possibly nonreduced structure.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1, printed p.35, finite-kernel argument

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated]. For a closed point $p\in P$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] gives $\kappa(p)=k$. If $A_p$ is nonempty, it has a closed point by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] applied to $A_p$, and this point is $k$-rational by the residue-field result. A choice $u\in A_p(k)$ identifies the whole scheme-theoretic fibre with $K$ by $v\mapsto v-u$, with inverse $w\mapsto u+w$. Thus every closed fibre is finite or empty. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fibre-dimension-upper-semicontinuous], the locus of fibres of dimension greater than zero is closed in $P$. If nonempty it contains a closed point by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], a contradiction. Hence every fibre has dimension at most zero.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.7(e): scheme-theoretic finite-kernel dimension argument, with closed-fibre extension supplied by the agent

proof.text: Now [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-image-dimension-bounds], with $d=\dim P$ and $n=0$, gives $g=\dim A\leq\dim P$. The identity is $k$-rational and $P$ is finite type. Its local ring is Noetherian, and [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension] identifies its Krull dimension with $\dim P$. The cotangent inequality [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] gives $\dim P\leq\dim_kT_0P=h$, since a finite-dimensional vector space and its dual have equal dimension. With step 2 this yields $g\leq\dim P\leq h\leq g$, so $h=g$. This also covers $g=0$; no smoothness of $P$ has been used.

source.place: I Remark 8.7(e), printed p.37: dimension comparison assembled from the two bounds

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q144-c59345d97 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement and the Milne sources in full: AV I Prop 8.1 (p.35), Remark 8.7(e) (p.37), and the construction before Lemma 12.2 plus the lemma itself (p.55). Only the split fields changed; the statement and blueprint fields are unchanged from the Q46 parent snapshot. There is no cycle: the item is absent from its 3624-node closure. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, the longest step is 1070 characters, and there is no SGA citation. Upper bound h<=g: Grothendieck vanishing kills H^q above g; the bialgebra node makes H^1 primitive; the primitive-product node makes g+1 independent elements multiply to a nonzero class in H^{g+1}=0. Lower bound g<=h: I recomputed the normalized family N on both identity axes and the cube quotient, so f is a homomorphism. The kernel argument follows Milne 8.1: B=(K_red)^0, then the (1,-1) pullback makes L|_B tensor [-1]^*L|_B trivial. Step 6 shows L|_B ample in the complete-linear-system sense (i = pi j, so j is a proper monomorphism and hence closed). Since H^0(O_B)=k, dim B=0. Closed fibres are translates of K, and semicontinuity plus Jacobson density bound every fibre. Then fibre bound g<=dim P = dim O_{P,0} <= dim m/m^2 = h, with no smoothness of P used, so the item avoids the parent's dim A^vee = g. Bialgebra node: true by Stacks 0BED (proper gives qc and separated), Koszul-sign multiplicativity, the counit from m(e x 1)=pr_2, and H^0=k from geometric integrality. Primitive-product node: true by projecting the iterated coproduct to multidegree (1,...,1) and applying dual coordinates, where only sigma=id survives; checked for r=2 and for characteristic 2. Both new nodes are statement-only, self-contained and searched. Neither duplicates an existing node (kunneth-qcoh, h1-product-spanning and wf-hopf-augmentation-height differ) or restates the item. The 17 generic tool_uses are accepted.
